passage:
"Bhaiya, how did you get through the audit without a single error?" Shankar asked.

"Honestly? I didn't. In my second year I missed a whole ledger, and my manager found it."

"You? But everyone says you never slip."

Madhav smiled. Hearing it felt good, he had to admit. "That is what they say. But it isn't true, and I would rather you know."

"So what do I do about the reconciliation?"

"Did you do it yourself? Then send it. Don't wait for me to check the first pass."

"What if it's wrong?"

"Then you will find out why, and that is worth more than my approval."

Shankar laughed, nervous and pleased, and went back to the desk.

qa.q: What did Madhav miss in his second year?
What was Madhav feeling when Shankar said everyone thinks he never slips?
qa.a: Madhav felt a little pride, since it felt good to hear, but he still chose to correct the picture.

qa.q: How does Madhav encourage Shankar's independence?
qa.a: He tells Shankar to send the reconciliation without waiting for him to check the first pass.

qa.q: How might Shankar feel after hearing about the missed ledger?
qa.a: Shankar may feel relieved and more confident, since even someone admired can make mistakes.

grounding: A mentor feels proud of a junior's admiration, shares a past failure honestly and encourages the junior to act independently.

passage:
Monday, late.

Gopika, the new intern, asked me today how I got so good at client pitches. She said, "Everyone says you're the best, sir." I felt about ten feet tall. I told her a long story about the Sharma account that made me sound like a genius. I left out the part where I nearly lost it.

On the drive home I felt a bit embarrassed. I'd enjoyed being looked up to a little too much. Was I helping her, or just polishing my own reflection?

So tomorrow, I'll tell her the real Sharma story: I misread the brief, the client almost walked out, and my boss saved me. That's where I actually learned.

And I'll stop answering every question for her. Next time she asks how to structure a deck, I'll ask, "How would you do it?" first.

I'm Lalit, and I'm not her hero. I'm her guide for a while. That's better.

qa.q: What did Gopika ask Lalit about?
qa.a: She asked how he got so good at client pitches.

qa.q: How did Lalit feel on the drive home?
qa.a: Lalit felt a bit embarrassed, aware of enjoying being looked up to too much.

qa.q: What will Lalit change in how he mentors Gopika?
qa.a: He'll share his real failure on the Sharma account and ask her how she'd do things first, to encourage her independence.

qa.q: How might Gopika benefit from hearing the real Sharma story?
qa.a: Gopika may feel less intimidated and learn that mistakes are part of growing, not a sign of failure.

grounding: A diary entry shows a young man who feels proud and self-important when an intern looks up to him, who decides to share his failures and encourage her independence.

passage:
Jasleen: Kishore bhaiya, can I send you my college application essay? you're the best writer I know 🙏
Kishore: sure, send it
Kishore: ok little sister, read it. it's good. really
Jasleen: you're just being nice
Kishore: no. the opening about your grandmother's sewing machine is great
Jasleen: can you just rewrite the ending? you'd do it so much better
Kishore: honestly, a bit of me wants to. I like being asked 😅
Kishore: but it has to sound like you, not me
Kishore: also, fun fact. my first college essay got rejected by 4 places. it was all fancy words and no me
Jasleen: WHAT. you??
Kishore: yep. so: what do you actually want them to know about you?
Jasleen: that I fix things. like Nani did
Kishore: then end with that. your words
Jasleen: ok. I'll try and send it tomorrow
Kishore: can't wait to read it 🙂

qa.q: How many places rejected Kishore's first college essay?
What does Kishore admit feeling when Jasleen asks him to rewrite the ending?
qa.a: Kishore admits feeling flattered and a bit proud, liking being asked.

qa.q: How does Kishore mentor Jasleen well?
qa.a: He shares his own failure, refuses to rewrite her work, and asks a question that helps her find her own ending.

qa.q: How might Jasleen feel after learning about Kishore's rejections?
qa.a: Jasleen likely feels surprised and relieved, seeing that even someone she admires struggled.

grounding: A chat shows a young man whom a younger person looks up to, who notices his pride, shares a failure honestly and encourages her independence.
